title: Gameplay from my solo boxing game inspired by 4D Boxing
author: DullSoil8917
selftext:
It’s been a while since my last dev update. Here’s some actual gameplay from the boxing game I’m making on my own.

It started with the classic boxing game *4D Boxing*. I wanted to capture that feeling of climbing the rankings one spot at a time and taking on the next opponent.

Every win earns you upgrade points, and before the next fight, you decide where to spend them. Do you make your punches hit harder, or build up your stamina so you can go the distance? I wanted players to be able to start with the same boxer and develop different fighting styles.

Once I had the climb up the rankings working, I wanted to give players a reason to look forward to the next opponent. So I started making regional champions, each with their own arena and signature move.

Yesterday I added a slow-motion knockdown replay. When a boxer hits the canvas, the game shows the punch that put them down from a different angle, then the count starts.

Slowing it down made me notice something that went by too fast during a fight: the opponent was already starting to fall before the glove even made contact. I reworked the animation from the point of impact through the end of the punch, and timed the sweat droplets to fly right on impact. What I really wanted to see in the replay was the moment that punch landed cleanly. There’s still plenty to fix, though. The glove still clips through the boxer’s face on some hooks, lol.

You can fight the regional champions now. There are still more champions and arena features to build, and I’m playing through fights and tweaking details like hit timing and camera work as I go.

This game started with the fun of picking your next opponent from the rankings. Lately, I’ve been thinking more about which moment will stick with you after a fight. I’ll keep working on it one moment at a time and share more gameplay clips along the way.
